healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Queen Elizabeth Hospital provides public healthcare. Private clinics and the Bayview Hospital cater to tourists. Good quality care for a Caribbean island. Tourists typically pay out-of-pocket.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is good by Caribbean standards. Queen Elizabeth Hospital is well-equipped. Private clinics offer comfortable, English-speaking care. The island is small so hospitals are always accessible. For complex specialized procedures, patients may be referred to Trinidad, Miami, or other international destinations.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturdays. Some pharmacies in Bridgetown and tourist areas have extended hours. Collins Pharmacy and Knights Pharmacy have multiple locations.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked with common medications. English is the national language so communication is easy. Prices are higher than mainland prices due to import costs. Sunscreen and after-sun products widely available. Bring specialized medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription requirements are enforced. Antibiotics require a prescription. Standard OTC medications are readily available. Controlled substances require a valid prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Carry doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal in Barbados. Do not bring any cannabis-derived products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English for controlled medications. Keep all medications in original pharmacy packaging. Barbados customs may ask about controlled substances.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended as healthcare costs are moderate to high. Important for water sports injuries, which are common. Medical evacuation to Miami or Trinidad may be needed for complex cases. Check coverage for scuba diving if applicable.

required: Yellow Fever (only if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required only when arriving from an endemic area. Routine vaccinations should be up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water in Barbados is safe to drink. The island has excellent water treatment infrastructure. Bottled water is available but not necessary. Coral-filtered natural water is the island's primary source.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are good. Fresh seafood (flying fish is the national dish), roti, and cutters (sandwiches) are staples. Restaurant hygiene is well-maintained. Street food from popular vendors is safe. Fish from reputable restaurants is fresh. Be mindful of excessive sun exposure while enjoying beach dining.
medicalTourismNote: Barbados is an emerging wellness tourism destination with spa and recovery-focused facilities. Fertility treatment clinics serve international patients. Not a major medical tourism hub for surgical procedures.
sources: Barbados Ministry of Health and Wellness

hospitals.name: Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Emergency department 24/7. Well-equipped by Caribbean standards. Full range of services.

hospitals.notes: Private medical center on the popular west coast. Convenient for Holetown and Speightstown area visitors.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available in Barbados. Several well-equipped private dental practices on the island.
dentalCare.costRange: $50-100 for consultation; $80-200 for fillings; $100-250 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is good quality but costs are moderate. Several modern practices in Bridgetown and along the south/west coast. English-speaking naturally.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental practices can usually accommodate emergencies. QEH also has a dental department for urgent cases.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 211 for emergencies; Barbados Association of Mental Health: +1 246-426-2657
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available. Barbados has English-speaking mental health professionals. Private therapists and the Psychiatric Hospital offer services.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available through both public and private providers. All services are in English. The Barbados Association of Mental Health provides support and referrals.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Barbados has made efforts to improve accessibility. Many newer hotels and restaurants are accessible. Beaches have limited wheelchair access. Bridgetown has some accessible infrastructure.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: QEH and Bayview Hospital are generally accessible with elevators and ramps.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses have limited accessibility. Taxis are the most practical option. Some hotels offer accessible transport. Beach wheelchairs available at select beaches.
accessibilityInfo.tips: The south and west coast hotel areas are generally more accessible than rural areas. Some beaches like Accra Beach have accessible facilities. Contact hotels and tour operators in advance about specific needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at clinics and QEH.
covidStatus.notes: Barbados has lifted all COVID-related entry restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics and QEH provide detailed receipts and medical reports in English. Insurance documentation standards are good. Keep all receipts. Some clinics may be able to bill insurance directly for larger claims.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Barbados dollar is pegged to USD at 2:1. Costs are moderate by Caribbean standards. QEH public rates are lower than private facilities.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Port of Spain, Trinidad or San Juan, Puerto Rico
medicalEvacuation.note: Barbados handles most medical cases locally. For complex specialized care, air ambulance to Miami is the standard route. Trinidad also has specialized facilities. Flight time to Miami is approximately 4 hours.
